comments.text:
Polish guy here 🇵🇱 
Since we're talking about the Haitian Revolution and the slave uprising, I'd like to remind everyone about the Poles who played a role in it.

At the time, Poland no longer existed as an independent country. It had been partitioned by Austria, Prussia, and Russia. Many Poles joined the Polish Legions formed in France because they believed that fighting alongside Napoleon would eventually help them liberate their homeland.

Instead, Napoleon sent them to Haiti to suppress the slave rebellion.

But when some of the Polish soldiers saw how the French were treating the enslaved Black population, they decided to stand with the oppressed. They switched sides, joined the Haitian revolutionaries, and fought against the French.

By making that choice, they knew they might never return to Poland, but they believed it was the right thing to do.

And the descendants of those Polish soldiers still live in Haiti to this day.
